headline: Boeing pays 2.5 billion dollars to settle MAX fraud charge
text: On 7 January Boeing agreed to pay more than 2.5 billion dollars to settle a US criminal charge that it hid information from safety regulators about the MAX: a 243.6 million dollar penalty, 1.77 billion dollars for airline customers and a 500 million dollar fund for crash victims' families.
imageCaption: The US Department of Justice headquarters, Washington

headline: The GameStop frenzy: small investors squeeze the hedge funds
text: Users of the Reddit forum r/wallstreetbets piled into GameStop, a struggling video game retailer, whose shares had been heavily sold short by hedge funds; the stock rose from 17 dollars at New Year to as much as 483 dollars on 28 January. The hedge fund Melvin Capital needed a 2.75 billion dollar rescue, and on 28 January Robinhood and other brokers stopped customers from buying the shares, causing an outcry. Trading volumes beat the peaks of 2008, and the market had its worst week since October.
imageCaption: GameStop store sign in New York at the height of the share squeeze, 27 January 2021
imageCredit: Photo by Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images

headline: A mob storms the Capitol
text: On 6 January, as Congress met to count the electoral votes, a crowd of Trump supporters stormed the US Capitol after a rally at which the president repeated his false claims of a stolen election; five people died. Congress certified Biden's victory the next morning. The House impeached Trump for a second time on 13 January, and Joe Biden was sworn in on 20 January.
imageCaption: Trump supporters crowd the west front of the Capitol during the attack, Washington, 6 January 2021

headline: Bezos hands over to Andy Jassy
text: On February 2 Amazon announced that founder Jeff Bezos will become executive chair in the third quarter and that Andy Jassy, head of Amazon Web Services, will become chief executive. Sales in 2020 rose 38% to $386 billion and fourth-quarter net income more than doubled to $7.2 billion.
imageCaption: Andy Jassy, who takes over from Jeff Bezos as Amazon's chief executive

headline: Payouts resume as copper soars
text: On 16 February Glencore reported flat 2020 adjusted EBITDA of $11.6bn, a net loss of $1.9bn after write-downs, and net debt down to $15.8bn, back in its target range. It will pay 12 US cents a share, about $1.6bn, resuming distributions. Copper averaged $8,471 a tonne in February, up from $5,183 last March.
source: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/glencore--glen/preliminary-results-2020/6364685; World Bank Pink Sheet monthly averages (both read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: An open-pit copper mine: Bingham Canyon, Utah
imageCredit: Doc Searls from Santa Barbara, USA

headline: Oil above 60 dollars lifts the drillers' suppliers
text: US crude passed 60 dollars a barrel in February for the first time in more than a year, closing the month at about 62, up from 52.
imageCaption: Drillships laid up at Las Palmas, Gran Canaria

headline: A 20 billion dollar loss, and the shares jump anyway
text: ExxonMobil reported on 2 February a fourth-quarter loss of 20.1 billion dollars, almost all of it write-downs; for 2020 as a whole it lost 22.4 billion dollars. But oil kept rising: US crude passed 60 dollars and closed February at about 62, up from 52 at the end of January. The company says it has cut costs faster than planned.
source: ExxonMobil press release of 2 February 2021, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/34088/000003408821000004/f8k4q991.htm (read 2026-10-03); https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DCOILWTICO (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ExxonMobil (2020 loss of 22.4 billion) (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Satellite view of ExxonMobil's Baytown refinery and chemical complex, Texas
imageCredit: NASA/METI/AIST/Japan Space Systems and US/Japan ASTER Science Team

headline: Greensill and Archegos in one month
text: On 1 March Credit Suisse froze four supply-chain finance funds with about $10 billion of assets, which it ran with Greensill Capital; on 4 March it decided to liquidate them, and Greensill filed for insolvency on 8 March. At the end of the month the US family office Archegos Capital failed to meet margin calls and its lending banks, Credit Suisse among them, began selling the positions they held for it.
imageCaption: Thomas Gottstein, chief executive of Credit Suisse

headline: Gelsinger returns and launches IDM 2.0
text: Pat Gelsinger, a former Intel engineer who ran VMware, became chief executive on 15 February after the board replaced Bob Swan; the shares rose nearly 8% when his appointment was announced on 13 January. On 23 March he announced a strategy called IDM 2.0: Intel will keep making its own chips, use outside factories where useful, and open a foundry business, Intel Foundry Services, to manufacture chips for other companies, with large new factories in the United States.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intel (read 2026-10-03); https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/50863/000119312521009142/d82915dex991.htm (read 2026-10-03, via search summary); https://edition.cnn.com/2021/01/13/investing/intel-new-ceo-pat-gelsinger/index.html (read 2026-10-03, via search summary)
imageCaption: Pat Gelsinger speaking at Web Summit, Lisbon, November 2017

headline: A 4.4-billion-franc hit from Archegos
text: Credit Suisse booked a provision for credit losses of 4,430 million francs for the first quarter on the Archegos default. The chief risk officer Lara Warner left on 6 April and the head of the investment bank, Brian Chin, stepped down; the board withdrew its pay proposal for the executive board and revised its dividend proposal. On 22 April the bank placed mandatory convertible notes of about 1.76 billion francs to rebuild capital. António Horta-Osório was elected chairman on 30 April.
imageCaption: Credit Suisse offices in the Uraniastrasse, Zurich

headline: The IEA says: no new oil fields
text: On 18 May the International Energy Agency published a roadmap to net-zero emissions by 2050. In its pathway no new oil and gas fields are approved beyond those already committed, and world oil demand falls to about 24 million barrels a day by 2050, from about 90 million in 2020.
imageCaption: IEA executive director Fatih Birol (left) with Italy's ecological transition minister Roberto Cingolani at the G20 meeting in Naples, 23 July 2021
imageCredit: Photo by FILIPPO MONTEFORTE/AFP via Getty Images

headline: Switzerland knock world champions France out of the Euro
text: At the European Championship, held a year late because of the pandemic, Switzerland came back from 1-3 down to draw 3-3 with world champions France on 28 June and won on penalties. It is Switzerland's first knockout win at a major tournament since 1938. They meet Spain in the quarter-final.
imageCaption: Switzerland v Wales at Euro 2020, Baku, 12 June 2021
imageCredit: Press Service of the President of Azerbaijan

headline: Evergrande, owing $300 billion, misses payments
text: China Evergrande, the country's most indebted property developer with about 2 trillion yuan ($310 billion) of liabilities, missed an interest payment of $83.5 million on foreign bonds on 24 September. Beijing's 2020 limits on developers' borrowing have cut off its credit.
imageCaption: People gather outside the Evergrande headquarters in Shenzhen as the developer warns of 'unprecedented difficulties', 14 September 2021
imageCredit: Photo by NOEL CELIS/AFP via Getty Images

headline: Hertz orders 100,000 Teslas and Tesla is worth a trillion
text: On 25 October the rental company Hertz said it will buy 100,000 Model 3s for its fleet, and Tesla's market value passed 1 trillion dollars for the first time, making it the sixth American company to reach that mark.
source: NPR, 'Tesla's market value hits $1 trillion after Hertz agrees to buy 100,000 of its cars', 25 October 2021, https://www.npr.org/2021/10/25/1048953565/hertz-will-buy-100-000-teslas-electric-vehicles (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc. (read 2026-10-03)

headline: GE will split into three companies
text: On 9 November General Electric announced it will divide itself into three listed companies, focused on aviation, healthcare and energy. The healthcare business is to be spun off first.
imageCaption: General Electric chief executive Larry Culp in a CNBC interview, 2019

headline: Inflation at 6.2 percent; the Fed starts to slow its bond buying
text: Consumer prices in October were 6.2 percent higher than a year earlier, the fastest rise since 1990. On 3 November the Fed said it would begin reducing its monthly bond purchases by 15 billion dollars, while still describing inflation as 'largely reflecting factors that are expected to be transitory'. Its rate remains near zero.
imageCaption: President Biden with Jerome Powell and Lael Brainard after announcing Powell would stay as Fed chair, Washington, 22 November 2021

headline: Daimler spins off its truck business
text: Daimler Truck, the world's biggest maker of heavy trucks, began trading on the Frankfurt stock exchange on 10 December as an independent company, after Daimler's shareholders voted for the spin-off on 1 October. What remains of Daimler is the Mercedes-Benz car and van business, and it plans to rename itself after its brand.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz_Group (read 2026-10-03); Daimler Truck press release 'Daimler Truck launched on stock exchange as an independent company', 10 December 2021, https://www.daimlertruck.com/en/newsroom/pressrelease/daimler-truck-launched-on-stock-exchange-as-an-independent-company-51850448 (via Google News, read 2026-10-03); CNBC, 'Daimler shareholders vote in favor of truck division spinoff', 1 October 2021 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03); data/src/universe.ts (spin-off factor) (read 2026-10-03)
